subject: Math
question_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mtext>Which of these quadrilaterals always has four equal sides and four right angles?</mtext></math>
solution_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mrow><mtext>Step 1: Recall the properties of a square. A square has four equal sides and four right angles.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 2: Compare with other quadrilaterals. A rectangle has four right angles but not always four equal sides. A rhombus has four equal sides but not always four right angles. A parallelogram does not always have equal sides or right angles.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Answer: Square</mtext></mrow></math>
question_text: Which of these quadrilaterals always has four equal sides and four right angles?
solution_text: Step 1: Recall the properties of a square. A square has four equal sides and four right angles. Step 2: Compare with other quadrilaterals. Answer: Square.

subject: Math
question_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mtext>How many vertices does a cuboid have?</mtext></math>
solution_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mrow><mtext>Step 1: A cuboid is a 3D shape with rectangular faces.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 2: Vertices are the corners of the shape.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 3: Count the corners of a cuboid. There are 4 corners on the top face and 4 corners on the bottom face.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 4: Total vertices = 4 + 4 = 8.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Answer: 8</mtext></mrow></math>
question_text: How many vertices does a cuboid have?
solution_text: Step 1: A cuboid is a 3D shape. Step 2: Vertices are the corners. Step 3: Count the corners: 4 on top, 4 on bottom. Step 4: Total vertices = 8. Answer: 8.

subject: Math
question_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mtext>What type of angle is greater than </mtext><mn>90</mn><mtext> degrees but less than </mtext><mn>180</mn><mtext> degrees?</mtext></math>
solution_mathml: <math xmlns='http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML'><mrow><mtext>Step 1: Recall the definitions of different angle types.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 2: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees. A right angle is exactly 90 degrees. A reflex angle is greater than 180 degrees.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Step 3: An obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>Answer: Obtuse angle</mtext></mrow></math>
question_text: What type of angle is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees?
solution_text: Step 1: Recall angle definitions. Step 2: An acute angle is < 90°, a right angle is = 90°, a reflex angle is > 180°. Step 3: An obtuse angle is > 90° and < 180°. Answer: Obtuse angle.
